折.meaning: An <part>anchor</part> pins down a huge map that won't close. An <part>axe</part> waits beside it. One whack straight down the middle, a sharp crease, and the map will finally <kanji>fold</kanji>.
折.on: A <sound>set</sound>ter dog grabs the folded map in its mouth and runs off with it.
折.kun: You fold the paper again and again until it's a tiny paper crane: <sound>ori</sound>gami.

合.meaning: An <part>umbrella</part>-shaped lid drops onto a <part>one</part>-plank rim over a <part>mouth</part>-shaped box. Click! Lid and box were made for each other: a perfect <kanji>fit</kanji>.
合.on: A <sound>goa</sound>t tries the lid on as a hat, and it fits the goat too.
合.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>! <sound>Ooh</sound>!' you say as the lid clicks into place.

羊.meaning: A <part>king</part> wakes up with curly <part>horns</part> poking out over his crown and wool sprouting down his back. His court tries very hard not to laugh. Overnight he has turned into a <kanji>sheep</kanji>.
羊.on: Stuck as a sheep, the king plays with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo all day to pass the time.
羊.kun: The sheep king charges at the guards' car and <sound>hits</sound> a <sound>jee</sound>p!

着.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> stands on top, and a long <part>slash</part> of yarn runs from its wool down past a big <part>eye</part> that never blinks. The eye watches you knit the yarn into a sweater, row by row. When it's done, you <kanji>don</kanji> it.
着.on: In your new sweater you dance the <sound>cha</sound>-cha, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the clock to watch.
着.kun: A brass <sound>key</sound> is knitted into the sweater's pocket, next to a little toy kanga<sound>roo</sound>.

遅.meaning: Under a <part>flag</part>, a <part>sheep</part> leads the parade down the <part>ramp</part>, stopping to nibble every patch of grass. The parade behind it crawls. Everything is <kanji>slow</kanji>.
遅.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah is stuck behind the sheep parade, panting with boredom.
遅.kun: You check the clock as the parade crawls by: '<sound>Oh</sound>! <sound>Cu</sound>ckoo!'

交.meaning: At a party, <part>father</part> wears a paper <part>lid</part> for a hat, his legs crossing as he shuffles from guest to guest. He shakes every hand and joins every chat. He loves to <kanji>mingle</kanji>.
交.on: Father hands every guest an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne as he passes.
交.kun: Father whirls his old mum across the floor. '<sound>Ma</sound>!' '<sound>Gee</sound>!' they shout.

安.meaning: A <part>woman</part> gets home, kicks off her shoes and flops onto the couch under her own <part>roof</part>. Phone off. Nobody needs her. At last she can <kanji>relax</kanji>.
安.on: Her <sound>un</sound>cle drops by, flops down on the other end of the couch and starts snoring.
安.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>!' she sighs, kicking off her shoes. '<sound>Sue</sound> me, I'm resting.' Lying here costs nothing.

円.meaning: A coin purse <part>frame</part> stands open. Inside, a <part>pole</part> rests on a <part>one</part>-plank shelf, with coins stacked against it. Bump the purse and they roll out across the floor, each one a perfect <kanji>circle</kanji>.
円.on: The coins spin so fast they roar like an <sound>en</sound>gine.
円.kun: One coin rolls under the couch. '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Roo</sound>'s got it!' yells the kid, as the pet kangaroo pockets the coin.

兄.meaning: A huge <part>mouth</part> on long <part>legs</part> struts around the house shouting orders at anyone smaller. Bossy, loud and a head taller than you: it's your <kanji>big brother</kanji>.
兄.on: Big brother eats the whole birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke before you get a slice.
兄.kun: He kicks you under the table to get the last crumb. '<sound>Ah</sound>! K<sound>nee</sound>!' you yell.

首.meaning: Two <part>horns</part> sit on a head that is nothing but a big <part>phone booth</part>, an <part>eye</part> peering out through its glass. It's so heavy that the poor creature needs a thick, strong <kanji>neck</kanji> to hold it up.
首.on: The creature bends its neck down to lick a pile of <sound>su</sound>gar cubes.
首.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo and a <sound>bee</sound> both perch on its long neck to sleep.

道.meaning: The horned creature stretches its long <part>neck</part> along the <part>ramp</part>, nose first, bumping every stone. Wherever it leads, it walks. Its trail becomes the <kanji>road-way</kanji>.
道.on: Along the road, the creature sniffs out a lump of bread <sound>dou</sound>gh.
道.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat and a <sound>chee</sound>tah race down the road after it.

好.meaning: A <part>woman</part> scoops up a <part>child</part>, who squeals and grabs her hair and won't let go. Both of them are grinning. They're very <kanji>fond</kanji> of each other.
好.on: She buys the child an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, and it ends up all over her hair.
好.kun: The child loves her toy koala so much that when you ask to borrow it, she hugs it tight: '<sound>Ko</sound>… <sound>no</sound>!'

小.meaning: A short hook stands in the middle, and two crumbs fall off on either side. A toddler holds up a cookie that has just snapped: tiny bits everywhere. Everything about it is <kanji>little</kanji>.
小.on: For the little ones there's a tiny puppet <sound>show</sound> on a cardboard stage.
小.kun: A cheetah cub, so little it can only squeak '<sound>chee</sound>-<sound>ee</sound>!'

歩.meaning: A <part>stop</part> sign up top. Below it, a <part>few</part> kids in a line, one short because he ran off. The rest stop at the sign, look both ways, and go on foot, one step, then another. That's how you <kanji>walk</kanji>.
歩.on: On the walk home, the kid stops for a <sound>ho</sound>tdog.
歩.kun: The dog walking beside the kid howls '<sound>Ah</sound>-<sound>roooo</sound>!' at the hotdog.

家.meaning: A <part>pig</part> moves in under your <part>roof</part>, takes the best bed and refuses to leave. It even hangs up a picture of itself. Now it isn't just your place: it's the pig's <kanji>house</kanji> too.
家.on: The pig fills the bath and keeps a big orange <sound>car</sound>p in it.
家.kun: When you ask the pig to leave, it squeals '<sound>Ee</sound>-<sound>eh</sound>!' and burrows under the blanket.

路.meaning: A <part>foot</part> stomps across the grass, stopping at <part>each</part> house in turn to knock with its toe. House after house, step after step, it wears a line into the grass: a <kanji>path</kanji>.
路.on: A little <sound>ro</sound>dent scurries along the path too, squeaking at each turn.
路.kun: Then a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p bumps along the path and makes it even wider.

主.meaning: A <part>king</part> wears a <part>lid</part> for a crown, with a single knob on top bigger than any other king's jewel. When he enters the hall, every other king bows. He's the <kanji>lord</kanji> of them all.
主.on: At the feast, the lord takes all the <sound>su</sound>gar cubes for himself.
主.kun: At every meal the lord spots a mole in his soup: '<sound>Oh</sound>! <sound>Mo</sound>le!'

味.meaning: A <part>mouth</part> waits beside a young fruit tree that's <part>not yet</part> grown: one short new branch sits above the long one. The mouth can't wait and bites a hard green fruit. Sour, sharp, strange: a <kanji>flavor</kanji> it has never had.
味.on: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat pops up beside the mouth to taste the fruit too.
味.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>gee</sound>!' says the mouth, juice running down its chin, and reaches for another.

力.meaning: One stroke bends like an arm with the elbow out, and a second stroke crosses it like a bulging <part>muscle</part>. Make a fist, flex, and feel the <kanji>power</kanji>.
力.on: A trio of strongmen toast with <sound>Rio</sound>ja, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock falls off the shaking wall.
力.kun: A cheetah flexes and lifts a whole car over its head as the crowd cheers: '<sound>Chee</sound>! <sound>Kah</sound>! <sound>Rah</sound>!'

田.meaning: A square split into four smaller squares, like farmland seen from a plane, with paths running between the plots. Each plot is flooded with water and planted with green shoots: a <kanji>rice field</kanji>.
田.on: A <sound>den</sound>tist sets up a chair in the middle of the field and pulls teeth among the shoots.
田.kun: The farmer shows off the four neat plots with a bow: '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!'

男.meaning: A farmer heaves a whole <part>rice field</part> over his head, his <part>muscle</part> bulging underneath it. Mud drips down his arms. That field-lifter, in this kanji, is the <kanji>male</kanji>.
男.on: Under the lifted field is a dripping <sound>dun</sound>geon, and its prisoners blink up at the daylight.
男.kun: He drops the field on a totem pole. '<sound>Oh</sound>!' he gasps as the <sound>to</sound>tem wobbles and a <sound>ko</sound>ala tumbles off the top.

東.meaning: At dawn the <part>sun</part> peeks through a <part>tree</part>, the trunk running right through it so the sun looks stuck on a branch. The sun always rises there, behind that same tree: in the <kanji>east</kanji>.
東.on: The rising sun warms your <sound>toe</sound> first as it pokes out of the blanket.
東.kun: At sunrise in the east, a knight wobbles out on tall <sound>hee</sound>ls, <sound>ga</sound>rlic round his neck, holding up his <sound>shie</sound>ld against the glare.

性.meaning: A gardener presses a stethoscope to a seedling bursting with <part>life</part> and listens to its <part>heartbeat</part>. 'Thump-thump… it's a girl!' she announces, like a vet with a new puppy. Every living thing has a <kanji>sex</kanji>.
性.on: The gardener locks the newborn sprout's papers in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe.
性.kun: A sprout's nature unfolds slowly, over years, like a long <sound>saga</sound>.

乙.meaning: Two runners race. One runs straight; the other runs a crazy <part>zigzag</part> across the track and, of course, comes in second. Of those two, the zigzagger is always <kanji>the latter</kanji>.
乙.on: The zigzag runner stops halfway to munch a bag of <sound>oats</sound>.
乙.kun: Zigzagging to the end, the runner crashes into a totem pole at the finish line: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' cries the runner, hugging the <sound>to</sound>tem.

雨.meaning: A flat sky line on top and a window frame hanging from it, with four drops running down the glass, two on each side of the bar. Look out of that window: it's <kanji>rain</kanji>.
雨.on: Rain drips into your bowl of <sound>u</sound>don, so the noodles never cool down.
雨.kun: The udon bowl overflows with rain, and you mutter '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>meh</sound>,' too gloomy to eat.

電.meaning: <part>rain</part> pours onto a <part>rice field</part>, and a <part>zigzag</part> of lightning hooks out of the bottom of the field, crackling. The field fizzes, and every bulb in the village lights up: <kanji>electricity</kanji>.
電.on: The village <sound>den</sound>tist plugs in her drill and it whirrs to life.

停.meaning: A <part>coat hook</part> sticks out of a roadside <part>pavilion</part>, a little roofed hut on a pillar where the bus waits. The bus driver hangs his cap on the hook, and the bus stops too. Everything comes to a <kanji>halt</kanji>.
停.on: Someone runs sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe right across the road, so nobody can move on.
停.kun: The bus halts nose to nose with a <sound>to</sound>tem pole. The driver shrugs: '<sound>Meh</sound>.'

付.meaning: A jacket hangs on a <part>coat hook</part>. A <part>golf club</part> swings in and whacks a sticker onto it, hard. It isn't coming off now: it will <kanji>adhere</kanji> to that jacket forever.
付.on: The sticker ends up stuck to your <sound>fu</sound>ton, and nothing will peel it off.
付.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' you sneeze as you stick a label on the <sound>ke</sound>ttle.

立.meaning: A dot of a head, a wide hat line, two little strokes for legs, and a long line of ground under them. Someone who was slumped in a chair has just jumped up. They <kanji>stand up</kanji>.
立.on: You jump up and a box of <sound>Ritz</sound> crackers tumbles off your lap.
立.kun: You stand up, bow and shout '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!', then sneeze '<sound>tsu</sound>!'

番.meaning: Farmers line up at the <part>rice field</part>, each holding out a <part>paw</part> full of seed. One by one they shake it out over the plots. 'Next!' Everyone waits for their <kanji>turn</kanji>.
番.on: Whoever's turn it is gets a sticky <sound>bun</sound> to eat while they sow.
番.kun: Two swans paddle up for their turn. One sneezes '<sound>tsu</sound>!' and the other gets <sound>ga</sound>rlic stuck in its beak, <sound>ee</sound>k: a pair.
